quotes.text: Section 11 is a by-product section: 'None is needed for Theorem A. All three are stated because they are genuine theorems.'

At $(75,125)$: $80/29$, so $\alpha = 80$, $q_{\mathrm{window}} = 29$, and the $y$-order cap $L(w) = \lceil \alpha w/q\rceil$ is superadditive off the period: $L(5) + L(24) = 14 + 67 = 81 > 80 = L(29) = \mathrm{ord}_y\Phi$, so no relation $c\Phi = eB$ can exist there.

Because $q_{\mathrm{window}} = 29 = M$ exactly, no split with $1 \le w < M$ is a multiple of $q_{\mathrm{window}}$, so the carry is $1$ on every admissible split and there is no weight at which the obstruction could vanish. ... So $(75,125)$ is more firmly obstructed by this mechanism than the earlier numbers claimed, not less.

Theorem 11.4 (criterion). Let $\alpha/q$ be $\mathrm{ord}_y(\Phi)/M$ in lowest terms, so $\gcd(\alpha,q) = 1$ and $q \mid M$; let $L(w) = \lceil\alpha w/q\rceil$ and $\mathrm{carry}(w_1,w_2) := L(w_1)+L(w_2)-L(w_1+w_2)$. For any candidate relation $c\Phi = eB$ with $c$ a nonzero constant and $w(e)+w(B) = M$, $1 \le w(e) < M$: $\mathrm{carry}(w(e), M-w(e)) = 0 \iff $q_{\mathrm{window}} \mid w(e)$, and the carry is exactly $0$ or $1$, never more.

Theorem 11.4 is a statement about the obstruction, not about existence: it shows that if the relation existed at $(75,125)$ then $(75,125)$ would have no lifts at all; the load-bearing negative there is a separate exhaustive search over exact identities, which is complete for ideal identities but not for membership in a radical or a saturation.

theorem_11_4.headline: Theorem 11.4 does NOT exclude (75,125). It is a criterion for the existence of the K-syzygy relation c*Phi = e*B. At (75,125), q_window = 29 = M and w(e) = 5, so no admissible split has carry 0; the relation cannot exist. The theorem therefore removes the (72,108) syzygy route at this corner; it says nothing about whether a Jacobian pair with these Newton polygons exists.
theorem_11_4.role: negative/diagnostic tool for the K-syzygy mechanism, not an obstruction to the (75,125) coefficient system
theorem_11_4.what_it_does_not_say: It does not say det J = x^2 is infeasible, and it does not exclude any (P,Q) with N(P)=3*Delta', N(Q)=5*Delta'.
theorem_11_4.research_note_claim: research/jacobian-degree-pairs-ge125.md:81 calls it 'a proved obstruction'. That is accurate only for the K-syzygy mechanism; it is not an exclusion of (75,125).

repo_status.quote: Theorem 2.1 is strict (max >= 125), so F_2(3,5)/125 sits *at* the bound and correctly stays open -- it is the unique row there, and the next increment of the bound depends on it alone.

full_lattice_sympy_cross_check.note: not run by default; --slow-cross-check runs config2_system.size_system on the full system (about 95-105 s measured)

timings.note: The exact bilinear accumulator expands the full 445-unknown system in well under a second; the measured SymPy expansion of the same determinant is about 13 s, and the full SymPy coefficient extraction is about 95-105 s (optional --slow-cross-check).

notes: No solving, elimination, Groebner basis, or collision search was performed.
det J is bilinear in the coefficients, so every nonconstant coefficient equation has total degree 2 in the unknowns.
The full-lattice system is overdetermined: 723 equations in 445 unknowns, or 723 in 443 after the two additive constants are removed.
The vertices-only system is 8 unknowns / 7 equations, but it is infeasible for det J = x^2 because the x^2 monomial is absent from det J; this is a support obstruction, not a Groebner obstruction.
No nonvanishing constraint is imposed on the vertex coefficients; solutions whose support drops to a smaller Newton polygon are included in the generic ansatz as boundary strata.
Theorem 11.4 is not an exclusion of (75,125); see theorem_11_4 above.
